subject: Close what a full browser pass of the app found
body:
Security and correctness on the API:
- /api/submitted settles a run only when the transaction's own
  TrajectoryAccepted log carries that run's hash; any successful protocol
  transaction used to settle any stored hash and issue it shares. The
  hash is normalised once, and an unknown run is a 404.
- The verifier refuses to sign for a task that is closed, past its
  deadline or minted (the contract records a signed run regardless), and
  answers 404 for a task id past the registry, 400 for a non-integer id.
- A whole-task dataset pull needs the subscriber's own signature, good
  for ten minutes; naming a subscriber's public address no longer
  downloads. An unreadable subscription contract now fails closed (503).
- The scheduled routes (reconcile GET and POST, snapshot, drill) close
  when CRON_SECRET is unset instead of opening to anyone.
- The x402 offer names the public URL, not the backend's localhost:8080.
- /api/feed clamps limit to 1..50 (−1 and 2.5 were 500s) and serves one
  contributor's whole history; /api/corpus bounds minScore; team POST on
  an unknown task is a 404, not a 500; the lab checks its receipt and
  reads the task id from its own TaskCreated log.

Pages:
- The company home drew the app's nav under its own: on Vercel the
  prerendered "/" hydrates as "/index". One normalised path hook now
  serves every component that asks where it is.
- Home, hub and floor agree on what is open: tasks taking runs now, not
  every unfilled slot on closed or expired tasks.
- /run/<unknown hash> and /task/007 are real 404s; 404 tabs say "Not
  found"; /localnet has its own title; an address in any letter case
  opens its operator page, which reads that operator's own runs.
- Corpus subscribers get a signed "Download task #N" and an honest time
  left ("24 h left", not "0 days"); /post computes escrow in wei, so a
  tiny reward posts instead of dying in parseEther; tiny MON amounts no
  longer print as 0.000; the practice button cannot open sign-in; the gas
  note names the floor it is raised at.
- Read failures say so on /task, /foundry, /licence and /space instead
  of "no such task", "no policy" or "every task is full".
- Copy that had drifted from the code: /contracts, the app home, the
  inventory's upload line, the corpus panel, /status explanations,
  README and SUBMISSION (Envio does not drive the feed).

browser; e2e expects a subscriber's bare address to be refused.

subject: Replace World ID with a passkey on Monad; the passkey also owns the robot; plain-language menus
body:
Operators are admitted by a passkey instead of World ID. The device makes
the passkey (Face ID, a fingerprint, a PIN) through Mera, Monad's passkey
library. Its P-256 key is registered in PasskeyRegistry from the operator's
own wallet. To join the CorpusShares whitelist, the passkey signs a
one-time challenge (/api/operator). The server checks the challenge,
origin, relying party and user verification. PasskeyRegistry then verifies
the signature on Monad through the P-256 precompile. /api/verify,
/api/sign and /api/submitted all read that whitelist.

- World AgentKit and AgentBook are gone. Agents pay per pull over x402 in
  USDC on Monad, and /api/agent/status now reports what a wallet bought.
- The old /passkey page used a WebCrypto key, not a passkey. It is now
  the real one, with a "prove it on Monad" read.
- The per-run passkey path is retired. The deployed Axon verifies
  sha256(trajHash), which a WebAuthn passkey cannot sign.
- The passkey owns the arm (the Mera "One Passkey, Many Keys" bounty). A
  PRF salt for "SO-101 commands" derives, via HKDF, an Ed25519 key in a
  Mera signing session. scripts/arm-relay.mjs --owner <key> moves the
  physical arm only for frames signed by it. An unsigned frame, another
  key, a stale timestamp or a replayed sequence gets STOP instead.
- The nav keeps every page, grouped into three menus (Earn, Data,
  Protocol) with a line on what each page is. On phones it is one Menu
  button. "Connect" is now "Sign in".
- README and SUBMISSION describe the passkey, and list the four bounties
  entered: Privy, Mera, Qwen 3.8 Max and Envio.

Tests:
- test/webauthn.test.mjs: the digest and DER arithmetic. With LIVE=1,
  PasskeyRegistry on Monad accepts a real assertion and refuses a
  tampered one.
- test/live-operator.mjs: every refusal the gate makes, over HTTP.
- test/live-passkey.mjs: Mera plus Chromium's WebAuthn authenticator. It
  checks the key, user verification, stable and separated PRF, and
  verification on Monad.
- test/live-arm-owner.mjs: the owner's passkey moves the follower;
  another passkey's frames stop it.
- test/arm-relay.test.mjs covers --owner.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Refuse to sign runs whose arm did not move the payload
body:
A scripted recording could leave the joints at zero while gliding the
payload onto the goal. It scored 100.00 and would have been paid in full.
The coherence check that caught it only ran at export time.

The signer now checks physicality before scoring:
- Every frame where a payload moves across the table must have a closed
  tool of some arm in the scene on it. The tool comes from that arm's own
  forward kinematics (THENAR-6, the second THENAR-6, or the SO-101).
- The payloads must begin where the task puts them. The start is read
  from the task on chain, and a scanned task's start is used when it has
  one.

A recording driven in the station passes by construction. A real run
recorded through the headset emulator passes; the scripted one is refused
with 422.

The signer also checks the human itself now. /api/sign refuses any
contributor that is not on the CorpusShares whitelist, which only a World
ID Selfie Check can put them on. Before this, anyone who could reach the
signer directly skipped the check that /api/verify makes.

subject: Let the issuer reclaim a dividend nobody can hold, and redeploy CorpusShares
body:
A dividend declared while no share exists is owed to nobody: at its record
date every holder's entitlement is zero, so no claim can ever succeed. The
first CorpusShares had no other way for that MON to leave, and the test
run's 0.01 MON dividend is still locked in it.

reclaimDividend returns what is left of such a dividend to the issuer,
only after the record date and only when the supply at that date was
zero. A dividend with holders is theirs and it cannot touch it. Three new
tests; on chain, a dividend was declared on the new contract, the record
date passed, and it came back in full, leaving the contract empty.

CorpusShares alone is redeployed by DeployShares.s.sol at 0xAE1F…0fc7,
exact_match on Sourcify; apply-deploy overlays it from that script's
confirmed broadcast. The first one is listed as superseded with the reason.

/corpus-token's event list now says it is this server's writes, which it
is: the issuer can also write from scripts/shares.mjs, and those are in
the figures above but not in that log.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Stop showing numbers nobody measured, and 404 what does not exist
body:
The first browser pass against the Monad deployment found pages stating
figures that were not readings:

- /operator reported "0 protocol calls, 0 reverted" whenever the index or
  the ledger failed, because a failure was stored as an empty list. It now
  says "—" and why, and "no runs" means only that.
- /post showed "Your balance 0.0000 MON" with no wallet connected, and
  projected the whole escrow as "scoring shortfall" from a mean score of
  zero when no run had been scored. Its gas note named "the six tasks
  here" after a seventh was posted; it now says what the receipts show.
- /task said a task "was posted with createTask" when it was posted with
  createTaskUntil and a zero deadline; it now says what the state shows.
- /handheld said the arm reaches 408 mm beside a spec sheet saying 512.
  Both are true of different things, so it now names the solver's reach
  and reads it from REACH_MAX.
- The manifest answered matches: false for a task with nothing committed,
  which reads as a mismatch. It is null until there is something to compare.

Pages that call Monadscan's index no longer ask when this deployment has
no key: next.config.ts exposes whether one exists, not the key, so an
unconfigured index is a stated reason rather than a 503 and a console
error on every load. A failure that does happen shows the server's own
sentence instead of "would not answer just now".

/station/999, /station/abc, /licence/<unminted>, /operator/nope were 200s
saying "not found"; they are 404s, asked of the contract the same way
/task asks, and still rendered when the chain does not answer.

/lab refetched its list once on the receipt, and on Monad the endpoint
serving the read can be a block behind the one that confirmed it, so the
list omitted the task the line above had just announced. It asks again
each second until the task is there. The Privy policy name is shortened
to Privy's 50-character limit, and the changelog is regenerated from this
repository's own history.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Deploy Thenar to Monad testnet
body:
Twelve contracts from DeployMonad.s.sol in one broadcast, seventeen
transactions, every receipt status 1, AxonProtocolV2 at block 64987386.
Five tasks seeded at 0.002 MON a run, six slots each, task 4 with a
seven-day deadline. The verifier is 0xC7D1…893D on the protocol and the
manifest; the corpus issuer 0x9a6A…e6b2 owns CorpusShares and SalesLog.
All twelve are exact_match on Sourcify for chain 10143.

apply-deploy.mjs now reads the newest record whose every transaction has a
successful receipt, not run-latest.json: forge wrote a second record a
minute after the broadcast, simulated against an endpoint that had not
caught up, with nonces five behind, addresses that belong to other
contracts and no receipts at all, and it overwrote run-latest with it.
Addresses are written checksummed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Write the Monad test plan, and answer an unconfigured snapshot with 503
body:
docs/TESTPLAN-MONAD.md lists every page, route, contract, integration and
flow with the exact result that counts as a pass, against the live Monad
deployment through a real browser.

The first sweep found /api/snapshot answering 502 when no bucket is
configured. 502 says an upstream failed, and here there is no upstream:
the drill already answered 503 for the same missing bucket. The snapshot
now answers 503 for no bucket and 502 only when a bucket refuses the
upload, and the OpenAPI document says both.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Script the demo take for the Monad build
body:
Every beat is confirmed from a Monad receipt with status 1 rather than a
mirror node or another chain's explorer: the lab's 0.004 MON bounty, the
policy's refusal, an agent's one-cent USDC pull with its SalesLog entry
read back through servedCount, and a dividend declared in CorpusShares.
The share beat is the dividend, not a run's issued shares, because a take
cannot produce a Selfie-Checked human. The intro names Monad Metropolis,
Track 4, and the pronunciations learn Monadscan and MON.

Nothing is recorded or voiced yet; tts.py has to run again before
cut.mjs, since the beat ids and the narration changed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Write the README and the Metropolis submission for the Monad build
body:
The README says what runs today and on which chain, what Monad does here
that another chain would not, and what is not proven. SUBMISSION.md makes
the case for Track 4 — identity, provenance, data ownership and agent
trust, each enforced by a contract — and says which commits existed
before Metropolis and which were written for it.

The Avalanche-era plans, audits and test reports move to docs/history,
where the Avalanche README already was. The Blitz audits keep their place
with a note that the project has come back to Monad on a new deployment.
.env.example names the keys the Monad build uses, and no contract
addresses, which live in lib/deployment.ts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Sell a task's corpus to agents over x402 in USDC on Monad, and log every sale on chain
body:
An agent asks /api/agent/corpus for one task's file and is answered 402
with two offers. One is x402's exact scheme on eip155:10143: a cent of
USDC as an EIP-3009 authorisation the agent signs, which the Monad
facilitator submits and pays the gas for. The other is AgentKit's: if
World's AgentBook maps the agent's wallet to a verified human, its first
three pulls are free, counted in the database so a restart does not hand
them out again. An agent with nobody behind it is not refused; it pays.

Settlement happens only after the export succeeds, so a task with nothing
recorded answers 404 and charges nothing. Every pull that succeeds is
hashed as served and written to SalesLog with that sha256. The log keeps
each sale in storage as well as in an event, because on Monad an event
more than a hundred blocks old cannot be read back through a public RPC,
and servedCount(sha256) lets a buyer check its own copy against the chain.

/agents states the terms the 402 states and lists every pull with its
settlement and its log entry. scripts/agent-buy.mjs is the buyer: it pays
from a wallet with USDC and no MON, hashes what it received and asks
SalesLog, not this server, whether those bytes were sold.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Gate paid runs on a World ID Selfie Check, and make the humans who pass it the corpus' only owners
body:
A paid run needs a live human behind the address. The station asks for a
Selfie Check before the run rather than after it, the proof and the
wallet's own signature have to agree, and a nullifier binds one person to
one address. It is asked on any chain, because it is a signature and a
phone scan, and a wallet that cannot add Monad must still reach it.

A proof that passes puts the address on CorpusShares' control list, and
every settled run issues its driver's shares, scaled by the signed score
and named by the run's hash. The contract refuses a share for anyone not
on the list, so a bot farm can record runs and cannot own the corpus.
On Monad both writes settle in under a second, so the station reports the
run's shares in the same panel as its payout instead of promising them.

/corpus-token reads the shares from the contract: supply, holders,
dividends, and whether it would accept a share for a given address, asked
by simulation. scripts/shares.mjs is the issuer's side: the register, the
compliance check, a dividend in MON with a record date two minutes out,
and one holder's entitlement.

The issuer key is not the verifier's. The verifier signs scores and lives
only in the signer service; minting shares is a different authority.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Sign operators in with Privy, and give labs a budget Privy can only spend on bounties
body:
An email address is enough to be paid: Privy makes an embedded wallet on
Monad, and an operator who already has a wallet can still bring it. When an
embedded wallet exists it is the active one, because some extensions sign
transactions but refuse to sign the plain message the Selfie Check asks for.

A lab's budget sits in a Privy server wallet under a policy with one allowed
action: a transaction to AxonProtocolV2 on chain 10143 carrying at most
0.1 MON. /lab posts a bounty from it and then asks the same wallet to send
0.01 MON somewhere else, so the refusal is something a lab can watch
happen. Privy signs; Monad's RPC broadcasts, with a gas limit of the
estimate plus a tenth, because Monad charges the limit.

scripts/privy-lab.mjs creates the policy and the wallet once, tops the
wallet up from the deployer, posts a bounty and prints the refusal.

This also brings in the dependencies the next commits use: Privy, World
IDKit and AgentKit, and x402 with its EVM scheme.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Move Thenar back to Monad, and read its history from storage
body:
Every page settles on Monad testnet again, chain 10143, where Thenar was
built at Blitz. MON is the bounty, the payout and the gas. The Foundation's
RPC is first, with Ankr and thirdweb behind it, each probed for batched
calls before being listed; drpc is left out because it refuses the gas a
Multicall3 read asks for.

Monad's public endpoints answer eth_getLogs only a hundred blocks wide,
under a minute of chain. The feed, the standings, the observed gas cost
and the mean score all read the log from the deployment block, so on
Monad every one of them would have been empty. They read the contract's
own arrays through Multicall3 instead, a hundred runs per call, each read
once because the array only grows, and a run's transaction is the one log
in the block the run recorded.

Per-address history comes from Monadscan through Etherscan's V2 API. It
needs ETHERSCAN_API_KEY, and without one the pages say that instead of
showing an empty history.

The registry reads its addresses from lib/deployment.ts, lists only the
contracts that have one, and names what each leans on Monad for: the
sharded slot counter for parallel execution, the P-256 precompile, and a
sales log kept in storage because events alone could not be read back.
The Avalanche L1 page and the Warp attestation go: neither exists here.

The QA and end-to-end scripts talk to the same chain through
scripts/monad.mjs, and scripts/monad-run.mjs records a scripted, paid run
with a gas limit of the estimate plus a tenth, because Monad charges the
limit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Put every contract on Monad in one broadcast, and give each run and task its block
body:
DeployMonad.s.sol deploys the whole set to Monad testnet in one go:
AxonProtocolV2, the passkey registry, certificates, the contribution
record, corpus access and manifest, referrals, the foundry, the prize pool
and confidential payouts, with five seeded tasks. The bounties are small
and set by REWARD_WEI, because Monad charges the gas limit and a deploy
estimated at 130% pays for the 30%.

Two contracts are new. CorpusShares is the corpus as shares: only an
address on its control list can hold, send or receive one, shares are
issued per run with the run's hash, and a dividend in MON pays whoever
held at a record date that has to be in the future when it is declared.
SalesLog records every corpus sale with the sha256 of the bytes served.
Both belong to a corpus issuer key, not the verifier.

A Trajectory now records the block it settled in and a Task the block it
was posted in. Monad's public endpoints answer eth_getLogs a hundred
blocks wide, so the app reads history from storage and finds a run's
transaction with a one-block query at the block the contract kept.

lib/deployment.ts is where the addresses live, written by
scripts/apply-deploy.mjs from forge's broadcast record, so no address is
ever typed in. scripts/monad.mjs gives every script the same chain.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Build the product on Avalanche Fuji
body:
Squashed from the 253 commits that took Thenar from Monad to Avalanche
Fuji and built the product there (8a90d40..2e1ac4d in thenar-io): the
station, the lab, the hub, policies, licences, referrals, the prize pool,
AxonProtocolV2 with escrow refunds and relayed passkey runs, the unit and
end-to-end suites, and the design system.

The Monad Blitz build is the history before this commit. What comes after
it is the move back to Monad.

subject: Point the repo at thenar.io and drop claims that no longer hold
body:
Every Railway URL in the docs, robots.txt and the scripts becomes the custom
domain. The one in vercel.json stays: it is the API proxy target, and the API
owns a SQLite file on a persistent volume that a serverless host cannot keep.

Also removes two things the README promised and the build no longer has: the
/passkey page, cut in 6111428 when wallet connect moved to RainbowKit, and
scripts/passkey-onchain.mjs, which does not exist. The precompile work is real
and stays documented against the fork tests that exercise it. Route count
corrected to ten, and the submission details are now a table at the top.

subject: README: correct the AxonProtocol test count
body: forge test reports 23, not 19; the suite grew with the sharding tests.

subject: README: inline demo GIF and a contracts section
body:
The video tag is stripped for some viewers, so the GIF carries the demo
inline and the release link carries the full cut. Adds the deployed
addresses, what each entry point does, and where the tests are.

subject: Embed the demo video in the README
body:
Recorded against the deployed build after the mirroring fix, so the payload
and the goal ring sit on the same side of the table as the arm reaching for
them. Both transactions in the cut are real and linked from the README.

subject: Un-mirror the payload, goal ring and trail
body:
The arm model is rotated -90 degrees about X, which maps its own plane-Y
onto three's -Z. The payload, the goal ring and the tool trail were all
placed from a plane-Y with the sign left positive, so every one of them
rendered mirrored across the table from the arm that was supposed to be
reaching for them.

The arithmetic was never wrong — the inverse kinematics land on the target
to the millimetre, which is why the grasp and the score worked while the
picture showed the block sitting on the opposite side, apparently untouched
and jumping about. Only the rendering carried the wrong sign.

subject: Fix space: auto-repeat was flipping the jaws back open
body:
Space toggled the jaws on every keydown, and a held key auto-repeats. One
press plus nine repeats — about half a second — flipped them open, shut,
open, shut and left them at 42 mm. Closing the jaws genuinely did nothing,
anywhere on the table, however close to the payload you were.

The toggle now ignores repeats, so one press is one change of state.

Space also activates whatever button has focus, and after Begin run that is
the End run button, so a press meant for the jaws could end the run instead.
Focus is dropped when a run starts.

subject: Stop the hero payload teleporting, and make the station payload graspable
body:
The hero attached the payload on the jaw opening alone, so the moment the
jaws closed the block snapped to the gripper from wherever it happened to
be, and at 76 percent of the cycle its resting place flipped from the pick
spot to the place spot in a single frame. Between those two it read as an
object floating around the table rather than one being carried.

It now rides the same keyframes as the arm — seated at the origin until the
grasp, carried until the release, seated at the destination after — and the
cycle alternates direction, so the loop never has to teleport it back to the
start.

The station's capture volume also reaches high enough that one press of Q
from the rest pose puts the jaws on the payload, and the readout says which
of the two things is wrong: how far away it is, or that you are over it and
too high.

subject: Make the payload actually graspable
body:
The capture test was a sphere measured to the payload's waist. The tool
cannot descend below 12 mm above the table and the waist sits at 37.5 mm,
so 25 mm of unavoidable vertical error came straight off a 55 mm budget and
left under 49 mm in the plane — and nothing on screen said whether you were
inside it, so finding it was guesswork. In practice the payload could not be
picked up.

The test is now a cylinder: within 90 mm in the table plane, and anywhere
along the payload's own height. The readout carries the distance to the
payload and turns to IN RANGE — PRESS SPACE once closing the jaws will
actually take it.

subject: Frame the hero arm from its real extent
body:
The camera sat about 1.08 m from an arm three quarters of a metre tall at a
32 degree field of view, so the hero was a close crop of the elbow — the
pick-and-place cycle it exists to show was off screen.

The distance is now solved from the arm's actual extent against the panel's
aspect, taking whichever of the two axes is tighter, so it frames the whole
cycle on a wide desktop panel and on a narrow phone one alike. Only the
distance is derived; the three-quarter view the product is drawn from is
unchanged.

subject: GSAP landing motion, step icons, canonical sitemap
body:
One authored sequence rather than scattered effects: the dimension rules
draw out from their centres, the headline settles, and the live chain
readings arrive last, because on a bench the measurement is the last thing
to appear. The run sequence reveals once as a batch on scroll.

Everything uses gsap.from, so the resting state is the visible one and
nothing is hidden if the script never runs, and the whole thing is skipped
under prefers-reduced-motion.

The four steps now carry drawn icons from the existing set, and the sitemap
points at thenar.io instead of the Railway backend, which would otherwise
have indexed every page twice.

subject: Revert the speculative viewport sizing changes
body:
Chased a blank station viewport that turned out to be the automation tab
being backgrounded: requestAnimationFrame is paused in a hidden tab, so
react-three-fiber never initialised its renderer and nothing mounted. The
canvas is fine in a visible tab.

viewport.tsx goes back to the version that was verified working, keeping
only the model path rename.

subject: Measure the station viewport off the settled layout
body:
The viewport is code-split and mounts under a grid row whose height is only
settled once the rest of the page has laid out. react-use-measure took its
first reading before that and fell back to 300x150, and because the row's
size never changed afterwards the observer had no reason to fire again.

Measuring undebounced off offsetWidth/Height reads the settled box, and one
dispatched resize on the frame after the GL context exists covers the case
where even that is early. RainbowKit's stylesheet also moved ahead of
globals.css in the layout, so its resets can no longer outrank Tailwind.
